name: Mesha
overview: The name Mesha appears in Scripture referring to multiple distinct entities, highlighting God's sovereign orchestration of history. Notably, Mesha was a king of Moab who initially paid tribute to Israel under Ahab but later rebelled after Ahab's death, illustrating the shifting political dynamics surrounding God's people (2 Kings 3:4-5). Additionally, Mesha is identified as a son of Caleb, linking him to the faithful lineage of Israel (1 Chronicles 2:42), as well as a Benjamite (1 Chronicles 8:9). The term also designates a geographical location associated with the Joktanites, emphasizing the broad cultural and historical context in which God's plan unfolds (Genesis 10:30).
